sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.desc: Hondius arrived Granadilla cargo port before dawn 10 May, escorted by Civil Guard vessel; anchored at sea with 1NM security perimeter — will not dock at pier. Evacuation commenced ~08:00 local via launch boats (max 5–10 pax), sealed army buses direct to Tenerife Sur airport; disembarkation by nationality only when respective repatriation flight confirmed runway-ready. No passengers showing symptoms as of 10 May morning. Skeleton crew of 30 to sail vessel to Rotterdam for full disinfection post-evacuation. German woman's body still aboard.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Confirmed source investigation zone. Index case (Dutch male, died 11 Apr) completed 4-month road trip spanning Argentina, Chile, Uruguay (27 Nov 2025–01 Apr 2026); returned from Uruguay to Argentina only 4 days before boarding. Tierra del Fuego Director of Epidemiology stated patients unlikely infected in province. Argentine Malbrán Institute conducting rodent trapping along travel route; Argentine national tally: 101 hantavirus infections since Jun 2025 — roughly double prior-year period.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr including Dutch index male's body and Dutch widow (later died Johannesburg) and Swiss confirmed male. UKHSA contact-tracing 30 disembarkees plus 82 pax and 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. Four Tristan da Cunha islanders also rode Hondius to St Helena per UK minister Doughty. Disembarkees from 12+ countries dispersed before hantavirus confirmed 02 May.

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, PCR+) died Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — confirmed Andes virus fatality. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU; condition improved and transferred to Netherlands. A second British national in a South Africa health facility confirmed PCR-positive 08 May. NICD contact-traced 65+ contacts from 25 Apr Airlink flight.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee, 56) transferred to Netherlands after improving in South Africa. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed German woman died of Andes virus. Three patients medevacked from Cape Verde to Schiphol 06 May; specialist teams received them in hazmat suits. KLM flight attendant tested PCR-NEGATIVE. RIVM classified event as level A2. Ship to proceed to Rotterdam post-Tenerife for full disinfection.

sites.name: LONDON
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed 2 British nationals PCR+ (one transferred to Netherlands, one confirmed 08 May in South Africa health facility) and one probable/suspected case on Tristan da Cunha (08 May). UK repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed. UKHSA also notes 4 Tristan da Cunha islanders rode Hondius to St Helena, expanding contact tracing scope.

sites.name: PARIS
sites.desc: Eight French nationals identified as close contacts of confirmed case on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight — none were on the cruise. One reporting mild symptoms, isolated pending PCR. French repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed via EU/national lift.

sites.name: ZURICH
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger disembarked St Helena 24 Apr via South Africa and Qatar; symptoms onset 01 May, tested positive Andes virus 05 May at University Hospital Zurich. Swiss confirmation 06 May raised total to eight cases at that point. Wife (also on trip) asymptomatic and isolating; Swiss authorities conducting additional contact tracing.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, pneumonia). Netherlands postmortem PCR confirmed Andes virus. Asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact evacuated 06 May to Netherlands, returned Düsseldorf, subsequently tested NEGATIVE. RKI contact tracing active. German repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed.

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: CLEARED (FIRST PCR): Centro Nacional de Microbiología confirmed first PCR NEGATIVE for the 32-year-old woman hospitalized in negative-pressure isolation — she sat two rows behind the deceased Dutch woman on 25 Apr Airlink flight. Per protocol, a second confirmatory PCR required 24 hrs later; if also negative, patient transfers to Gómez Ulla Military Hospital, Madrid as contact-quarantine. Status downgraded from suspected to monitor pending second PCR.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius arrived Granadilla 10 May; evacuation operation underway described by Health Minister García as 'unprecedented.' WHO DG Tedros personally on island overseeing operation alongside Spain's health, interior, and territorial policy ministers. 358 Guardia Civil agents involved; waterfront cordoned, reception tents erected. Canary Islands president Clavijo, despite prior objections, receiving vessel; local port workers held protests. Canary Islands authorities want ship and all passengers departed by end of 10 May.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Gómez Ulla Military Hospital activated to receive 14 Spanish Hondius passengers (13 pax + 1 crew per Oceanwide manifest). Spanish nationals first to disembark; transferred by sealed army buses to Tenerife Sur airport, flown Madrid for military hospital quarantine. PCR on arrival + Day 7; twice-daily temperature monitoring; individual rooms, no visitors. Alicante woman to transfer here if second PCR negative.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: Two Barcelona contacts monitored: (1) South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent ~1 week here before returning to South Africa — confirmed asymptomatic. (2) Barcelona-resident woman identified 09 May as flight contact after initially escaping detection due to mid-flight seat change; asymptomatic, placed under official monitoring per Spanish Health Ministry.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed probable case 08 May: British male islander who was aboard Hondius during 13–15 Apr Tristan da Cunha stop; symptoms onset 28 Apr, currently stable in isolation on island. UK Minister for Overseas Territories Stephen Doughty wrote to island administration confirming patient is 'an islander' and spouse is isolating. Four additional islanders had ridden Hondius to St Helena, expanding contact tracing scope.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: CLEARED 09 May: Both male residents (aged 67 and 65) tested NEGATIVE for hantavirus including Andes virus via multiple PCR samples — Singapore CDA confirmed. Both had disembarked Hondius at St Helena and traveled on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. Monitoring continues as precaution through full incubation window.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home early, asymptomatic. Four Canadians total remain aboard vessel awaiting Tenerife evacuation. PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 10 May. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states; all 17 Americans still aboard as of 10 May test negative and asymptomatic per CDC.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH monitoring one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident remains aboard ship and will transit Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC/HHS biocontainment charter. No California residents reported ill or infected as of 10 May.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Georgia DPH monitoring two residents who returned from Hondius. Both in good health with no signs of infection as of 10 May. Following CDC recommendations. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic as of 10 May. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. CDC classified response as Level-3 (lowest emergency activation tier); Emergency Operations Center activated. Six states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA, NJ — monitoring at least 9 early-disembarkees or contacts.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ health authorities monitoring two individuals potentially exposed to a Hondius passenger post-disembarkation during air travel. Neither symptomatic as of 10 May. Part of broader US monitoring cohort per CDC reporting.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC National Quarantine Unit (NQU) fully staffed and activated. CDC/HHS charter inbound from Tenerife with 17 American Hondius passengers — all PCR-negative and asymptomatic. CDC confirmed: NO mandatory quarantine; passengers assessed at NQU then may opt for 42-day home self-monitoring with at least daily contact with state/local health departments. NQU has 20 spaces with negative airflow rooms.

sites.name: UTAH
sites.desc: Utah DHHS confirmed at least one Utah resident among the 17 Americans aboard MV Hondius. Person is asymptomatic and will disembark Tenerife then travel with federal escort to Nebraska NQU for evaluation. No Utah residents monitored at home as of 10 May.

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none currently ill as of 10 May. Skeleton crew of ~30 will remain aboard to sail vessel to Rotterdam; most crew to be repatriated from Tenerife. Monitoring continues.

sites.name: DUBLIN
sites.desc: Two Irish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed via EU Civil Protection Mechanism aircraft. Irish Dept of Health coordinating with ECDC and WHO; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored off Praia 03–06 May; departed 19:15 local 06 May for Tenerife. Three medevac patients evacuated here 06 May — two flew to Amsterdam (received by specialist teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled refueling stop at Gran Canaria after Morocco refused permission and a medical equipment malfunction caused delays. Cape Verde assessed unable to handle full passenger evacuation.

sites.name: COPENHAGEN
sites.desc: Danish Patient Safety Authority confirmed one Danish national was aboard MV Hondius. Person returned to Denmark end of April, is self-isolating, displayed no symptoms, and was not in close contact with any confirmed cases. Monitoring active per national protocol.

sites.name: BRUSSELS
sites.desc: Belgian nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Repatriation from Tenerife via EU Civil Protection Mechanism aircraft confirmed. Belgian federal health authorities coordinating with ECDC. No symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WELLINGTON
sites.desc: New Zealand confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius per WHO/CBS News 08 May. NZ Ministry of Health coordinating contact tracing; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: STOCKHOLM
sites.desc: Sweden confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius. Swedish Public Health Agency (Folkhälsomyndigheten) coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ANKARA
sites.desc: Turkey confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius. Turkish Ministry of Health coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: BASSETERRE
sites.desc: Saint Kitts and Nevis confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who had disembarked MV Hondius. Local health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ATHENS
sites.desc: Greek nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Greece among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). Greek Ministry of Health coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported. Monitoring of returning nationals underway.

sites.name: WARSAW
sites.desc: Polish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Poland among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). Polish Chief Sanitary Inspectorate coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: LISBON
sites.desc: Portuguese nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing (Portugal among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board). DGS Portugal coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.
